mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of rising unemployment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate activity, measured by a 5% rise in housing starts over two months, signals strong economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of rising housing starts compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 2% over two months signals a contraction in supply, which leads to reduced corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of declining industrial production compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal: a high level of real personal consumption expenditures (above $400 billion) indicates strong consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when RSAFS is above $400 billion compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal: when the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when both conditions are met compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal: when nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.3%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher when both conditions are met compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal: during a late-cycle expansion, a decline in GDP growth rate by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in late-cycle expansions with declining GDP growth compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
